title: RAW UNREVIEWED: a rare copied drawing anomaly may bind an entry before any word gloss
summary: Seek a dated, named illustrated source entry that shares with an admitted Voynich plant not merely a broad taxon silhouette but a rare, anatomically odd arrangement of at least three attached structures. Inventory the anomaly in a fixed image-only comparison against a full same-witness plant deck before reading target text; require a second witness or explicit source stemma to rule out common iconographic convention. If one independently named source owner survives, freeze its complete entry-specific organ, preparation and use relations and compare two whole target readings with opposing consequences. Generic visual resemblance, a modern species guess and a text fit chosen after seeing the source do not count. No exemplar or plant identity is currently asserted; failure to find a diagnostic anomaly is missing source capacity, not a negative word test.

design.mechanism: a rare inherited illustration anomaly anchors a source entry independently of Voynich text, enabling its written relations to challenge complete candidate readings
design.unit: one independently named pre-1500 source entry, its same-witness image deck, a second stemmatic witness, and one complete admitted Voynich plant record
design.contrast: source-specific organ/preparation/use relation versus a rival complete reading that shares the pictured plant but reverses or omits that relation
design.prediction: only a prospectively fixed multi-feature anomaly and independently owned source relation can distinguish whole readings; broad silhouette alone leaves missing binding
